newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ukraine has most of draft Russia white sugar quota.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine has most of draft Russia white sugar quota.

text.p: The Russian Foreign Trade Ministry has sent an order to the government setting white sugar imports at 1.5 million tonnes per year, Tass quoted deputy minister Oleg Davydov as saying on Thursday.
The Ukrainian annual allowance in the draft quota would be 1.15 million tonnes, Tass added.
Davydov was quoted as saying the quota, which had been under consideration for a number of months, was temporary and would give Russian producers a chance to get used to competition.
"The measure is temporary and after a certain period of time the barrier will be withdrawn."
Agricultural officials have said cheap Ukrainian sugar has flooded the Russian market, putting pressure on domestic producers, who have had difficulty adjusting to market reforms.
Tass did not say when the quota, which must be approved by the government, would come into effect.

Ukraine, Russia's primary source for whites, sent 1.6 million of its 1.9 million tonnes of refined sugar exports during the 1995 crop year to Russia, an official Ukrainian trade analysis centre said on October 9.

It expected Ukraine -- which is forecast to produce three million tonnes of whites from domestic beet from this year's crop, down from 3.5 million last year -- would export 1.5 million tonnes from this year's crop to all destinations.
Russia has a glut of whites even though the market has already been protected by import tariffs, which traders say make whites imports from Europe and Brazil unprofitable.
